title: Roadhouses and sitting in for beer
summary: Hinton and Maxwell compare playing roadhouses and country dances for tips and sitting in for free.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Surely. I can remember around Chicago, we had quite a few places to play, naturally, in Chicago. But the younger guys like myself at that time, you know, early thirties, the younger guys like us couldn't get a job in town. And we used to get in the car and go out to what they called roadhouses. That's the little saloon out on the highway, we'd just unpack and go in and start playing. If people would give us a couple bucks, we stayed.
That's what we did, too, yeah.
If they didn't give us anything, we'd go down the road to the next place.

That's what I did. Or I would go out by myself. I didn't have a car but if I could get a friend to take me out to one of these roadhouses or just out to one of the country dances, I would go in if they had arrangements or if they didn't have arrangements I'd say, look, let me sit in and play solos. I'll play for nothing, couple of beers or something, just -- I remember doing that many times.
